points.description: States the core repeated process: selection sort finds (selects) the minimum element of the array/unsorted part and places it at the first position, then repeats on the remaining part, placing the next minimum at the second position, and so on.
points.partial_credit: 2 to 3 marks if only one half is stated, e.g. finds the minimum and puts it first but does not say it repeats on the rest, or the idea is vague or has a minor error.

points.description: Makes clear that the next minimum is chosen from the remaining (unsorted) part of the array and goes to the next position (second, third, ...), continuing until sorted.
points.partial_credit: Half a mark if repetition is mentioned without saying it works on the remaining part.

rubric.notes: Full marks for stating that selection sort repeatedly picks the minimum of the unsorted part and puts it in the next position, in any wording, even briefly. Part marks if the student only says it finds the minimum and places it first, or describes the idea vaguely. No marks for describing a different sort (e.g. swapping adjacent elements as in bubble sort) or only naming the algorithm without its mechanism.
